content:
The image shows split soybean stems/roots laid on soil. Key features:

- Stems are split lengthwise revealing the internal pith
- The pith appears bleached/white in most sections
- There is a dark mass of black sclerotia visible in the central stem cavity — hard, black, irregular bodies packed inside the stem
- The outer stem tissue is bleached white/gray
- No fluffy white mycelium visible on the outside, but the internal black sclerotia are the hallmark feature

This matches **White Mold** (Sclerotinia stem rot): the characteristic black sclerotia embedded within the bleached white stem interior is the definitive diagnostic feature. The stems are split to show the sclerotia inside — exactly as described ("hard, black sclerotia resembling rodent droppings on or inside stems").

This does not match Charcoal Rot (which has microsclerotia giving a charcoal-sprinkled appearance externally, with grayish streaks) or Sudden Death Syndrome (white pith but no sclerotia).
